correctness.rationale: P=KG(5,2), ten vertices and fifteen edges, colored supports A,B may overlap. A color-support S forces its antineighborhood Phi(S) into the other support; singletons force six; adjacent pairs force four and nonadjacent pairs force three. Thus any 2-rainbow assignment of weight<=5 must have supports (2,3) or (3,2), with nonadjacent 2-set A and B=Phi(A). Verify representative A={12,13}, Phi(A)={14,15,23}, Phi(B)=A, five empty vertices both-color dominated, and S5-transitivity. All 30 nonedges yield two named orientations=60 minima of weight five; unique forced counterpart forbids any individual-color jump and hence slide. Independently rebuilt KG(5,2), enumerated all 4^10 labelings and single-color transitions; agrees with 60 and frozen configurations. Exact fixed graph, not an asymptotic extension.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Tong et al 2009 general GP(n,2) minimum weights is stronger in graph family but weaker on optimizer multiplicity and reconfiguration. The k>=3 Kneser 2k theorem has incompatible color count.

originality.rationale: Known 2009 Tong–Lin–Yang–Luo theorem establishes gamma_r2(GP(5,2))=5; that scalar is excluded from the new claim. The 2024 full cubic-rainbow paper primarily proves t=3..5 bounds; the published multi-rainbow Kneser theorem assumes k>=3 and cannot imply a named two-color optimizer census. A search did not find the mutual antineighborhood bijection or absolute single-color immobility in inspected results; this is best-of-knowledge only. The full 2009 original remains unavailable after authorized retrieval; possible implicit classification in its proofs is a substantive residual risk.

value.rationale: The canonical smallest generalized Petersen graph is a natural benchmark for two-resource domination. The complete characterization of all cheapest named-color placements and their frozen one-resource reconfiguration geometry adds structural information not implied by its known minimum weight; the 30 independent-pair to path antineighborhood duality explains the rigidity. It is a complete natural finite classification, not merely a checksum or arbitrary subset.
